title: Let users take over product-world camera without adding another camera authority

scope.subject: Reuse the existing camera-controls input/actions and controlstart lifecycle so System/Orbit/Surface become manually explorable and user camera input interrupts an active Journey

research_summary: Personal Universe already uses @react-three/drei CameraControls backed by camera-controls v3.1.2 for all product-world cinematic shots, but CinematicCamera explicitly maps every mouse/touch action to NONE. This prevents manual exploration after arrival and means Journey can be interruptible through navigation buttons but not through direct camera takeover. The installed camera-controls implementation already provides ACTION.ROTATE/DOLLY/TOUCH_DOLLY_ROTATE, a controlstart event, and—critically—its drag start code stops the relevant in-progress rotate/dolly movement by synchronizing end state to the current camera state. Drei v9.122.0 directly forwards camera-controls controlstart/controlend as onStart/onEnd. Reuse this same controller rather than add OrbitControls: enable target-preserving rotate/dolly input for stable System/Orbit/Surface phases, mark the cinematic shot as manually overridden on controlstart, clear settled evidence, and notify UniverseApp to stop any active Journey. Approach/Atmosphere/Returning remain cinematic so manual input cannot leave a half-completed cross-scale transition.

sources.finding: The exact installed camera-controls version exposes ACTION input mappings and controlstart; startDragging synchronizes active rotate/dolly end state to current state, naturally interrupting the corresponding programmed movement instead of requiring another controller.
The exact installed Drei CameraControls wrapper forwards controlstart/controlend to onStart/onEnd and mounts the same CameraControlsImpl instance used for programmatic transitions.
Pinned MIT TourPlayer treats competing camera navigation as tour interruption, supporting the product rule that explicit user camera takeover should stop Journey orchestration rather than fight it.
React Three Fiber remains the single shared Canvas/camera host; manual control must stay on that camera rather than create another render or navigation surface.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep the existing YEIS/Personal Universe spatial product and reuse its interruption principle; the product-world camera itself is already intentionally owned by the R3F layer.
Keep the single R3F Canvas and camera lifecycle.
Reuse TourPlayer's user-navigation-interrupts-tour semantic; do not port its old state machine or UI.
Reuse the exact existing CameraControls instance, ACTION mappings and onStart event. Adding OrbitControls or a second camera component would create competing camera state.

candidates.name: Existing camera-controls v3.1.2 manual input on the same cinematic controller
candidates.reason: Already owns all product-world camera transitions and directly provides rotate/dolly/touch input plus user-control events; using it preserves one camera state and lets user input naturally interrupt current movement.

candidates.name: Add Drei OrbitControls beside CinematicCamera
candidates.reason: Would create a second controller mutating the same camera, duplicate target/distance state and require arbitration with existing cinematic transitions.

candidates.name: Project-owned pointer/touch orbit implementation
candidates.reason: Duplicates mature camera-controls pointer, touch, damping, distance and transition-interruption logic already shipped.

decision.rationale: Enable only the existing CameraControls instance. System/Orbit/Surface get left-drag rotate, wheel/middle dolly and touch rotate/pinch-rotate with no truck/pan so the destination target remains authoritative. controlstart marks the current cinematic shot as manually overridden, removes settled evidence and notifies UniverseApp; an active Journey is stopped immediately so orchestration never fights the user. Approach/Atmosphere/Returning remain input-disabled cinematic transitions.
decision.fallback: If free dolly proves too permissive in runtime visuals, narrow min/maxDistance per phase while keeping the same CameraControls authority; do not add another controller.
